items.title: Des préservatifs rappelés après un risque de défaillance, les utilisateurs appelés à la vigilance
items.description: Une vaste opération de rappel concerne des préservatifs commercialisés sous la marque «My Lubie» en France entre décembre 2025 et mai 2026. L'information, largement relayée et commentée par des médias locaux, fait état d'un risque de défaillance pouvant favoriser la transmission d'infections sexuellement transmissibles (IST) ou une grossesse non désirée. Les consommateurs sont invités à ne plus utiliser les produits concernés. Une alerte sanitaire a été lancée en France à propos des préservatifs vendus dans plusieurs enseignes de distribution, pharmacies et plateformes de commerce en ligne. L'information, abondamment reprise par de nombreux médias, s'appuie sur une publication du site officiel Rappel Conso, qui annonce le retrait de certains lots jugés non conformes. Selon l'avis de rappel publié le lundi 3 août, ces préservatifs présentent «un produit non-conforme et un risque microbiologique», une situation susceptible d'entraîner un «risque de transmission d'infections sexuellement transmissibles (IST) ou de grossesse non désirée». Les produits concernés sont des boîtes de 12 préservatifs ultra-fins en latex naturel, de taille standard, commercialisés sous la marque «My Lubie». Selon les informations diffusées, ces préservatifs ont été mis en vente entre le 23 décembre 2025 et le 22 mai 2026. Ils étaient disponibles dans plusieurs réseaux de distribution, notamment chez Monoprix, Passage du Désir, Nuoo, dans des pharmacies à travers la France, ainsi que sur des plateformes de vente en ligne telles qu'Amazon, Mademoiselle Bio et Ayanature. Face à cette situation, les autorités recommandent aux personnes ayant acheté ces produits de ne plus les utiliser et de suivre les consignes de rappel afin d'éviter tout risque pour leur santé sexuelle. Ce nouveau rappel illustre l'importance des contrôles de qualité sur les dispositifs de protection sexuelle. Les consommateurs sont invités à vérifier les références des produits qu'ils détiennent et à rester attentifs aux avis publiés par les autorités compétentes, d'autant que cette alerte a suscité un large écho dans les médias en raison des conséquences potentielles sur la santé publique. Par Valentin SOMANDE L’article Des préservatifs rappelés après un risque de défaillance, les utilisateurs appelés à la vigilance est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

items.title: Coopération sino-guinéenne : la Chine remet 20 bourses d’études et réaffirme son amitié avec la Guinée
items.description: L’Ambassade de la République populaire de Chine en Guinée a organisé, ce mardi 4 août 2026, une cérémonie officielle de remise des lettres d’admission aux vingt bénéficiaires guinéens des bourses du Gouvernement chinois, au titre de l’année universitaire 2026-2027. Ces étudiants poursuivront leurs études dans plusieurs universités chinoises de renom, dans des filières stratégiques telles que les mines et les technologies, les sciences électroniques et technologiques, l’aéronautique, l’économie et la finance, les infrastructures routières, la diplomatie, l’économie et le commerce international, ainsi que le domaine maritime. Prenant la parole, Sun Yong, ambassadeur de la République populaire de Chine en Guinée, a d’abord souhaité la bienvenue aux invités ayant pris part à cette cérémonie marquant le départ des boursiers guinéens du Gouvernement chinois pour l’année universitaire 2026-2027. Au nom de l’Ambassade de Chine en Guinée, il a adressé ses chaleureuses félicitations aux nouveaux lauréats appelés à poursuivre leurs études en Chine. « Je suis convaincu que chacun d’entre vous a choisi d’étudier en Chine avec curiosité, enthousiasme et confiance envers ce pays. Le développement de la Chine vous ouvrira également une fenêtre privilégiée sur une autre culture et vous permettra d’élargir votre horizon international. Sous la direction du Parti communiste chinois, la Chine a réalisé les deux grands miracles que sont une croissance économique rapide et une stabilité sociale durable. Les réalisations de la modernisation chinoise suscitent aujourd’hui l’attention du monde entier », a-t-il déclaré. Poursuivant son intervention, le diplomate chinois a mis en exergue la solidité des relations sino-guinéennes, fondées sur plusieurs années de coopération et de confiance mutuelle dans de nombreux domaines. « La Chine et la Guinée entretiennent une amitié traditionnelle. La Guinée est le premier pays d’Afrique subsaharienne à avoir établi des relations diplomatiques avec la Chine nouvelle. La Chine est un véritable ami et un véritable frère de la Guinée. Depuis l’établissement de nos relations diplomatiques, nos deux pays ont toujours adhéré aux principes du respect mutuel, de l’égalité et du soutien réciproque, avançant main dans la main face aux défis comme sur la voie du développement. Des centrales hydroélectriques aux routes, des projets d’alumine au projet de Simandou, de nombreux projets de coopération mutuellement bénéfiques ont vu le jour, créant de nombreux emplois, contribuant à prolonger les chaînes de valeur locales et à transformer les ressources naturelles de la Guinée en moteur de développement, tout en insufflant une forte dynamique à son industrialisation et à la diversification de son économie. Parallèlement, les entreprises chinoises implantées en Guinée s’investissent activement dans les communautés locales, organisent des formations professionnelles et assument pleinement leur responsabilité sociale, contribuant ainsi à l’amélioration du bien-être de la population et au renforcement de l’amitié sino-guinéenne », a-t-il ajouté. Évoquant la coopération dans le domaine de la formation, l’ambassadeur a rappelé les nombreux programmes destinés aux cadres et étudiants guinéens, qui ont déjà touché des centaines de personnes. « Chaque année, la Chine accueille également plus de 300 responsables gouvernementaux et techniciens guinéens dans le cadre de programmes de formation couvrant des domaines tels que la diplomatie, l’économie, l’agriculture et la médecine. De plus en plus de jeunes Chinois et Guinéens se rencontrent, échangent et grandissent ensemble, insufflant une nouvelle vitalité à l’amitié entre les deux pays. Grâce notamment aux Bourses du Gouvernement chinois, près de 700 jeunes Guinéens talentueux ont déjà poursuivi leurs études en Chine. En outre, près de 1 000 étudiants guinéens choisissent chaque année d’y effectuer des études à leurs propres frais », a-t-il rappelé. L’ambassadeur Sun Yong a également précisé que, pour cette nouvelle promotion, dix-sept étudiants bénéficieront de la Bourse du Gouvernement chinois, tandis que trois autres recevront la Bourse chinoise du secteur des transports. « 17 étudiants bénéficieront de la Bourse du Gouvernement chinois et 3 autres de la Bourse chinoise du secteur des transports, prenant ainsi le relais de cette belle tradition d’amitié. À l’avenir, la Chine et la Guinée continueront d’approfondir leur coopération dans les domaines de l’éducation et des échanges humains, d’encourager davantage de jeunes à renforcer leurs échanges et leur compréhension mutuelle, afin que l’amitié sino-guinéenne se transmette de génération en génération et apporte un nouvel élan durable au développement des relations bilatérales », a-t-il déclaré. S’adressant directement aux bénéficiaires, il leur a adressé trois recommandations majeures. « Premièrement, je souhaite que vous soyez des ambassadeurs de l’amitié sino-guinéenne. Saisissez pleinement cette opportunité d’étudier en Chine, nouez de solides amitiés, découvrez la richesse de la culture traditionnelle chinoise ainsi que les réalisations de la modernisation chinoise, et devenez des passerelles entre les peuples chinois et guinéen. Deuxièmement, je souhaite que vous étudiiez avec assiduité et développiez de solides compétences. La jeunesse s’épanouit dans l’effort. Je vous encourage à chérir ces précieuses années d’études, à apprendre avec sérieux, à développer vos talents et à faire en sorte que vos études portent pleinement leurs fruits. Troisièmement, je souhaite que vous respectiez les lois et les règlements afin de mener un séjour d’études sûr et serein. La sécurité est la condition première de la réussite de vos études. La Chine est un État de droit où chacun est égal devant la loi. Je vous invite à respecter scrupuleusement les lois chinoises ainsi que le règlement de vos établissements, à renforcer votre vigilance en matière de sécurité et à faire de votre séjour un parcours sûr, sain et exemplaire, pour vous-mêmes comme pour rassurer vos familles », a déclaré l’ambassadeur de la République populaire de Chine en Guinée. Représentant le Premier ministre, chef du Gouvernement, Saïkou Oumar Baldé, conseiller principal, a pour sa part transmis la reconnaissance du Gouvernement guinéen à la République populaire de Chine pour son engagement constant en faveur de la formation de la jeunesse guinéenne. Il s’est ensuite adressé aux bénéficiaires, les invitant à mesurer la responsabilité qui les attend tout au long de leur parcours académique. « Chers étudiants, je voudrais m’adresser à vous particulièrement. À partir d’aujourd’hui, vous serez les ambassadeurs silencieux de notre pays. Chaque salle de classe que vous fréquenterez, chaque laboratoire où vous travaillerez, chaque bibliothèque que vous parcourrez et chaque rencontre que vous ferez contribueront à façonner l’image de notre pays. Confucius nous enseignait que “l’homme de bien exige tout de lui-même, mais l’homme médiocre attend tout des autres”. C’est cette pensée qui doit devenir votre discipline quotidienne. N’attendez jamais que les circonstances décident de votre destin, ne restez pas à l’écart. Décidez vous-mêmes de la hauteur à laquelle vous voulez élever votre existence ; on vous en donne l’occasion avec ces bourses. Observez la société chinoise. Apprenez la langue, apprenez la culture, apprenez la diversité. Vous partez étudier à l’étranger, cela ne signifie jamais partir pour rester. Vous partez pour acquérir des compétences et revenir servir dignement votre pays », a-t-il déclaré. Poursuivant, il les a exhortés à incarner l’excellence et l’intégrité afin d’honorer l’image de la Guinée à l’étranger. « N’oubliez jamais que le talent est une promesse, mais que seul le travail en fait une réalité. Que le savoir impressionne, mais que le caractère inspire. Que les diplômes ouvrent les portes, mais que l’intégrité ouvre les consciences. Je vous invite également à découvrir avec curiosité et respect la Chine. Son Excellence Monsieur l’Ambassadeur l’a mentionné, il y a un certain nombre de règles et de principes qui régissent le fonctionnement de l’État chinois. Vous devez être les ambassadeurs de la République de Guinée en vous soumettant à toutes les lois et obligations de la République populaire de Chine. Et Sénèque rappelait que “ce n’est pas parce que les choses sont difficiles que nous n’osons pas, c’est parce que nous n’osons pas qu’elles sont difficiles”. Osez apprendre, osez entreprendre, osez exceller, osez représenter dignement la République de Guinée. C’est l’image de notre pays qui est en jeu », a-t-il souligné. Présent à cette cérémonie, Aboubacar Camara, directeur général du Service national des bourses extérieures (SNABE), a salué l’engagement constant du Gouvernement chinois en faveur de la formation des cadres guinéens. « Cette coopération éducative entre nos deux pays, ancrée dans une relation d’amitié ancienne et une confiance mutuelle solidement établie, constitue l’un des piliers les plus tangibles du partenariat stratégique global qui unit la République de Guinée et la République populaire de Chine. Je voudrais, à cet égard, rappeler que la promotion de l’excellence académique est le credo de Son Excellence le Président Mamadi Doumbouya, Président de la République. C’est dans le droit fil de cette vision que s’inscrivent les efforts constants déployés par le Gouvernement, à travers le SNABE, pour offrir à la jeunesse guinéenne les meilleures opportunités de formation à l’étranger », a-t-il déclaré. Le directeur général du SNABE a également rassuré les bénéficiaires du soutien permanent de l’État guinéen tout au long de leur cursus. « Je voudrais également, à cette occasion, rappeler que le Gouvernement guinéen, à travers le SNABE, accompagnera votre parcours et demeurera attentif à votre situation tout au long de votre formation. Nous comptons sur vous pour honorer, par votre travail, la confiance qui vous est faite. À votre retour, la Guinée aura besoin de vos compétences pour poursuivre son développement, singulièrement dans les domaines couverts par la coopération sino-guinéenne, qu’il s’agisse des infrastructures, des transports, de l’industrie ou du commerce », a-t-il ajouté. S’exprimant au nom des bénéficiaires, Hawa Mara, porte-parole des étudiants pour la circonstance, a exprimé la reconnaissance des bénéficiaires envers les Gouvernements chinois et guinéen, ainsi qu’à l’ensemble des institutions ayant contribué à la concrétisation de ce programme de bourses. « Nous exprimons notre profonde gratitude au Gouvernement de la République populaire de Chine pour son engagement constant en faveur de la formation des étudiants guinéens. Nos remerciements vont également au Gouvernement guinéen, au Service national des bourses extérieures, ainsi qu’à toutes les institutions qui ont contribué à rendre ce projet possible. En nous apprêtant à rejoindre les universités chinoises, nous prenons l’engagement de faire preuve de sérieux, de discipline et d’excellence. Nous serons des étudiants exemplaires, mais également des ambassadeurs de la Guinée, respectueux des valeurs de notre nation et de celles du pays qui nous accueille. À notre retour, nous mettrons les connaissances et les compétences acquises au service du développement de notre pays, convaincus que l’avenir de la Guinée se construit aussi grâce à une jeunesse bien formée », a-t-elle promis. Mamadou Yaya Barry & Robert Kourouma L’article Coopération sino-guinéenne : la Chine remet 20 bourses d’études et réaffirme son amitié avec la Guinée est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .

items.title: Four rescued after minibus crashes near GRA office at Circle
items.description: A Hyundai minibus carrying four men crashed near the Ghana Revenue Authority (GRA) office at Circle on Tuesday, leaving two occupants injured as firefighters mounted a rescue operation to free those trapped in the wreckage. According to the Ghana National Fire Service (GNFS) Public Relations Officer for the Greater Accra Region, the Circle Fire Station received a distress call at 12:41 p.m. reporting the crash. Firefighters were dispatched a minute later at 12:42 p.m. and arrived at the scene by 12:44 p.m., where they immediately began rescue and emergency response operations. The accident involved a Hyundai minibus with registration number AS 3198-Y, which sustained extensive damage to its front bumper and driver’s side. “Upon arrival, personnel encountered severe structural impact resulting in total damage to the vehicle’s front bumper and driver’s side,” the GNFS said in a statement. Firefighters rescued all four occupants trapped in the vehicle. Two of the men sustained injuries and were treated at the scene before being stabilised for further medical evaluation. The statement said the firefighters “rescued four men from the wreckage, with two injured male victims promptly attended to and stabilized for medical evaluation.” After completing the rescue, emergency personnel secured the accident scene and worked to eliminate any hazards to ensure the safety of other road users. The GNFS said its operational team also restored safety along the affected stretch of the road while investigations into the cause of the crash continue. Motorists have meanwhile been urged to exercise caution and comply with road safety regulations to help reduce road traffic accidents.

items.title: Arrestations présumées à Kati, les experts appellent à renforcer la confiance entre les FAMa et les populations
items.description: Plusieurs presumes terroristes auraient ete interpelles a Kati entre le 2 et le 3 août par les forces de defense et de securite. Les autorites n'ont pas encore communique sur cette operation. Pour les specialistes, la collaboration entre les FAMa et les populations reste un levier essentiel pour prevenir et combattre le terrorisme. Pour Alhousseiny Guindo, analyste securitaire, la lutte contre le terrorisme repose aussi sur une relation de confiance entre les forces de defense et les citoyens. « Le militaire est un civil en mission pour lutter efficacement contre le terrorisme. L'etablissement et le renforcement de la confiance entre les forces de defense et de securite et la population sont indispensables. » Selon l'expert, cette cooperation permet aux populations de partager des informations utiles et d'alerter les autorites en cas de menace. Prevenir les attaques L'analyste estime qu'une bonne collaboration entre les FAMa et les populations peut contribuer a empecher des attaques avant le passage a l'acte des hommes armes. « Ce qui pourrait resulter d'une telle collaboration reside dans la prevention et dans l'evitement de toute attaque terroriste, voire de toute suspicion d'attaque terroriste. » Il rappelle que les renseignements fournis par les habitants peuvent faciliter les interventions des forces de defense et de securite dans les localites. Renforcer la confiance des populations Pour encourager cette cooperation, l'analyste securitaire insiste sur la necessite d'instaurer un climat de confiance. « Pour rendre cette collaboration facile, il ne faut pas que la population voie en ses forces de defense et de securite des dangers pour elle. Que quelqu'un qui denonce ou qui indexe des zones susceptibles de danger ne se voie pas etre pris comme etant lui-meme une personne dangereuse. » Ainsi, selon Alhousseiny Guindo, les citoyens doivent pouvoir signaler des zones suspectes sans craindre des represailles. Cette confiance constitue un element cle pour ameliorer la prevention et renforcer la lutte contre le terrorisme. Lire aussi : L'armee annonce plusieurs frappes contre des groupes armes L’article Arrestations présumées à Kati, les experts appellent à renforcer la confiance entre les FAMa et les populations est apparu en premier sur Studio Tamani - Informations, débats, magazines : toute l’actualité du Mali, en 5 langues .

items.title: Houet : 943 recrues de la troisième vague du contingent 2025 officiellement intégrées aux Forces armées nationales
items.description: Houet : 943 recrues de la troisième vague du contingent 2025 officiellement intégrées aux Forces armées nationales Bobo-Dioulasso, 04 août 2026 (AIB) – Les 943 recrues de la troisième vague du contingent 2025, dont 30 femmes, ont été officiellement présentées au drapeau, ce mardi au camp Ouezzin-Coulibaly de Bobo-Dioulasso, à l'issue de vingt semaines de formation militaire initiale, marquant leur entrée dans les rangs des Forces armées nationales. Présidée par le commandant de la 2ᵉ Région militaire et commandant d'armes de la place de Bobo-Dioulasso, le lieutenant-colonel Lassané Porgo, la cérémonie a consacré l'engagement solennel des nouvelles recrues à servir la Nation avec discipline, loyauté et patriotisme. Dans son allocution, le commandant du Groupement d'instruction des Forces armées (GIFA), le chef de bataillon Honoré Bè Palm a indiqué que les 943 recrues, dont 30 femmes, incorporées le 3 avril 2026, ont suivi une formation militaire initiale de quatre mois, axée sur l'adaptation, l'aguerrissement et la consolidation des acquis. Cette formation, orientée vers les exigences de la lutte contre le terrorisme, a porté notamment sur le combat, le tir, le secourisme, les techniques d'intervention opérationnelle rapprochées, les techniques d'action immédiates et la sensibilisation aux engins explosifs improvisés. S'adressant à la presse à l'issue de la cérémonie, le lieutenant-colonel Lassané Porgo a souligné que la présentation au drapeau constitue une étape majeure dans la vie d'un militaire : « C'est la première fois que ces soldats sont officiellement acceptés dans les rangs. Ils prêtent serment devant le peuple, devant leurs familles et devant la hiérarchie de défendre la patrie jusqu'au sacrifice suprême », a-t-il expliqué. Il a invité les nouvelles recrues à rester fidèles à leur engagement, à faire preuve de discipline, de patriotisme et d'une confiance totale envers leur hiérarchie afin de contribuer efficacement à la défense du territoire national. Au nom des recrues, le délégué de la troisième vague du contingent 2025, le soldat de deuxième classe Abdoul Razack Compaoré, a exprimé sa fierté d'avoir franchi cette étape: « En ce jour, je suis animé par le sentiment d'être allé au bout de mes limites, d'avoir surmonté la peur et la fatigue. Je suis très heureux d'avoir intégré la grande famille militaire, d'arborer l'insigne, l'uniforme et le béret durement gagné », a-t-il déclaré, assurant que ses compagnons d'armes et lui sont désormais prêts à défendre le Burkina Faso. La cérémonie s'est achevée par des démonstrations pratiques illustrant le savoir-faire acquis durant la formation. Les nouvelles recrues ont exécuté des exercices de montage et de démontage rapides d'armes, avant de simuler la riposte tactique à une embuscade visant un camion militaire, démontrant ainsi leur réactivité et leur préparation opérationnelle sur le terrain. Agence d'Information du Burkina KS/CS/AB/wis

items.title: Transport routier : nouvelle tranche de soutien exceptionnel aux professionnels
items.description: Le ministère du Transport et de la Logistique a annoncé le lancement d’une nouvelle tranche de soutien exceptionnel direct au profit des professionnels du transport routier de personnes et de marchandises, couvrant la période allant du 16 au 31 juillet 2026. Cette nouvelle tranche intervient suite à la décision du gouvernement de poursuivre l'octroi de ce soutien exceptionnel afin d'accompagner les fluctuations rapides des prix des carburants sur les marchés et son impact sur le marché national, a indiqué le ministère dans un communiqué. L'inscription pour bénéficier de cette nouvelle tranche sera ouverte dès jeudi 06 août 2026 via la même plateforme numérique dédiée: https://mouakaba.transport.gov.ma , précise-t-on. items.title: Police investigate deaths of two women found in Tamale hotel, IGP deploys special team
items.description: The Ghana Police Service has launched investigations into the deaths of two women whose bodies were discovered in a hotel room in Tamale, with the Inspector-General of Police (IGP) deploying a special team to support the probe. According to a press release issued by the Northern Regional Police Command on Tuesday, August 4, the bodies were found in a room at Cab Hospitality Hotel in the Gbewa Residential Area of Tamale on Monday, August 3, 2026. Police said they responded to the scene after receiving a report from the hotel management and found the bodies of the two women, who are believed to be nationals of Benin. The bodies have since been conveyed to the Tamale Teaching Hospital Mortuary, where they will undergo preservation and a post-mortem examination to establish the exact cause of death. The Police said preliminary investigations are underway to determine the circumstances surrounding the deaths, establish the identities of the deceased, and liaise with the relevant authorities to facilitate contact with their families. To strengthen the investigation, the IGP has deployed a special team comprising investigators, intelligence officers and crime scene personnel from the National Police Headquarters to assist the Northern Regional Police Command. The Police have appealed to members of the public with credible information that could assist the investigation to contact the Police through the emergency numbers 191 or 18555, or report to the nearest police station.

items.title: Transporters demand lower taxes and diesel prices, threaten wheel-jam strike from Aug 8
items.description: ISLAMABAD: The All Pakistan Goods Transporters Alliance on Tuesday announced a nationwide wheel-jam strike from Aug 8, warning that the suspension of freight movement could disrupt the supply of essential commodities if the government failed to address its demands. The announcement was made at a press conference at the National Press Club by the alliance’s leaders, including All Pakistan Goods Transport Owners Association President Muhammad Owais Chaudhry Advocate, Malik Shafeeullah Awan and Malik Nisar. They said the transport sector was facing an unprecedented financial crisis due to repeated increases in diesel prices, higher taxes and other government measures. The transporters demanded that taxes on diesel be reduced and fuel prices be restored to their July 1, 2024, level. Demands were also issued for a reduction in the withholding tax on cargo transporters from seven per cent to 2pc, arguing that oil tanker operators were already paying only 2pc. The alliance also rejected a provision introduced in the Finance Act 2026 under which an entire vehicle could be confiscated if non-duty-paid goods were found on board. Describing the measure as unjust and demanding its immediate withdrawal, the transporters urged the government to restore the previous system under which fines were imposed and vehicles released. They also sought uniform implementation of axle-load regulations across the country, saying overloading should be checked at factories, warehouses and loading points rather than through roadside enforcement, which they alleged had become a source of revenue collection. Among other demands, the transporters called for a simpler procedure for obtaining heavy transport vehicle driving licences, a reduction in toll taxes and an end to the daily adjustment of diesel prices. They demanded that fuel prices be revised fortnightly or monthly to provide greater certainty for transport operators. All Pakistan Goods Transport Owners Association President Muhammad Owais Chaudhry said the current policies had pushed drivers, small transporters and vehicle owners paying instalments on financed trucks into severe financial hardship, making it increasingly difficult for them to continue operations. “We have repeatedly approached the government through letters, meetings and media appeals, but no meaningful progress has been made,” he said. It was jointly announced that unless the government entered into immediate negotiations and accepted their demands, all categories of goods transport, including cargo trucks, containers and oil tankers, would remain off the roads from Aug 8. The alliance leaders said the strike would remain peaceful, adding that transporters would park their vehicles instead of blocking highways. However, Malik Nisar warned that a prolonged shutdown could significantly affect imports, exports and the transportation of essential goods, adding that the government would bear responsibility for the consequences.

items.title: Youth Ministry partners DTI to build industry-ready workforce for Ghana
items.description: Three-year collaboration to strengthen industry-led skills development, entrepreneurship and workplace readiness The Minister for Youth Development and Empowerment, George Opare Addo, and the President of the Design and Technology Institute (DTI), Constance Elizabeth Swaniker, on Tuesday, August 4, 2026, signed a landmark three-year Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) aimed at building an industry-ready workforce capable of driving Ghana’s industrialisation and economic transformation. The strategic partnership between the Ministry of Youth Development and Empowerment (MYDE) and DTI seeks to align youth skills development with the evolving needs of industry by expanding access to practical training, entrepreneurship, internships and workplace readiness programmes. Speaking at the signing ceremony, George Opare Addo described the collaboration as a strategic investment in Ghana’s future, stressing that the country’s youthful population remains its greatest national asset and that equipping young people with relevant skills, values and opportunities is essential to national development. He observed that many young Ghanaians continue to grapple with challenges including limited labour market opportunities, inadequate access to information, skills mismatch, weak technology and start-up support, and youth health concerns. According to him, addressing these challenges requires stronger collaboration between government and institutions with proven expertise in skills development and innovation. Under the agreement, MYDE will provide policy leadership and coordinate implementation through national youth development platforms, while DTI will contribute its expertise in competency-based training, curriculum innovation, workforce development and industry engagement. The collaboration will expand opportunities in technical and vocational education, structured internships, entrepreneurship development and digital skills training to ensure that young people acquire competencies that respond to the demands of today’s labour market. A key pillar of the partnership is the adoption of DTI’s Precision Quality framework, which promotes professionalism, productivity, quality consciousness, workplace discipline and safety. The framework is expected to produce graduates who are not only technically competent but also equipped with the work ethic and professional standards increasingly required by employers. The programme will also focus on strengthening communication, teamwork, leadership, critical thinking, customer service, emotional intelligence and financial literacy to enhance the overall employability of young people. Entrepreneurship support, mentorship, coaching and business incubation will equally form part of the collaboration to encourage more youth to become job creators. The Minister noted that the partnership would complement existing national youth development initiatives by fostering greater collaboration and expanding opportunities rather than duplicating ongoing interventions. To ensure sustainability, both institutions will jointly mobilise support from government, development partners, the private sector and international organisations to scale up youth-focused skills and employment programmes. Mr. Opare Addo expressed confidence that the partnership would translate into practical programmes and measurable outcomes that would produce a skilled, innovative and resilient workforce capable of supporting Ghana’s long-term socio-economic transformation.

items.title: Les chèques sans provision continuent de fragiliser les TPE
items.description: Les chèques sans provision reviennent au centre des débats, les réformes engagées ces dernières années pour moderniser leur régime juridique n’ont pas allégé l’impact des incidents de paiement qui continuent de peser lourd sur l’activité des très petites entreprises (TPE). Les dernières données publiées confirment que le phénomène reste bien présent, alors que les professionnels appellent à des solutions capables de mieux sécuriser les transactions commerciales. Les TPE premières exposées, souffrent souvent de déséquilibre de trésorerie déjà fragile avec chaque chèque rejeté ou retard de paiement des fournisseurs. Etant donné qu’elles sont des structures disposant de marges financières limitées, quelques impayés suffisent parfois à mettre en difficulté l’activité. Une situation qui intervient alors que de nombreuses entreprises continuent de composer avec un coût du financement élevé et une demande encore irrégulière. Ces dernières années, les pouvoirs publics ont adopté plusieurs mesures afin de réduire les incidents de paiement et d’encourager leur régularisation mais le problème persiste, alors que les professionnels restent prudents et rappellent que la confiance demeure un élément essentiel dans les relations commerciales, notamment entre les petites entreprises. Un chèque sans provision ne représente pas seulement un litige entre deux parties, il peut entraîner une série de difficultés pour l’entreprise créancière, partant des tensions de trésorerie jusqu’au report de certains projets. Sur ce point, plusieurs observateurs estiment que la prévention reste tout aussi importante que les mécanismes de sanction et les procédures de privation de carnet de chèques voire l’incarcération. Pour l’heure, la question reste entière. Les réformes ont permis d’adapter le cadre juridique, mais reste à savoir si elles suffiront à réduire durablement le nombre d’incidents. Les prochains mois seront déterminants pour mesurer leurs effets sur le terrain et leur capacité à renforcer la confiance dans les moyens de paiement utilisés par les très petites entreprises. The post Les chèques sans provision continuent de fragiliser les TPE appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

Qatar says progress made toward US-Iran talks on ending war
items.description: Qatar said mediators were making progress in efforts to end the US-Iran war on Tuesday, driving oil prices lower, although Tehran has denied President Donald Trump’s assertion that talks are already under way. Benchmark Brent crude fell more than four per cent after the comments from Qatar, extending Monday’s steep losses on hopes that an arrangement could soon be reached to restore traffic through the blockaded Strait of Hormuz. But for now, the strait remained virtually shut, with another ship reportedly coming under attack while trying to cross it. Trump said on Monday that talks with Tehran had started and Iran faced a “last chance” to reach a deal. Iranian officials insisted no negotiations with the United States were taking place. Iran says its only talks are with Oman about the strait, and that no major meetings were planned this week. But senior US officials struck an optimistic tone on Tuesday, with Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Secretary of State Marco Rubio both pointing to progress in discussions aimed at reopening the Strait of Hormuz, a corridor that normally carries about a fifth of global oil and liquefied natural gas shipments. “There’s been progress made in those talks, but not finality yet. We’re hoping that will happen very shortly,” Rubio told reporters at the State Department. Bessent said a deal with Iran on the reopening of Hormuz could be reached by Tuesday or Wednesday. Qatar’s foreign ministry spokesperson Majed al-Ansari said diplomatic contacts had reached “very progressive stages”. He said mediators including Qatar, Pakistan and Oman were coordinating closely to facilitate negotiations and exchange draft proposals between Washington and Tehran. Trump’s comments followed his weekend decision to cancel what he described as “massive attacks” on Iran, extending a pattern in which he has threatened major military action before later backing off and pointing to diplomatic contacts. Shipping risks remain Iran has halted most traffic through Hormuz while Washington maintains a blockade of Iran-related shipping and ports. Yemen’s Iran-aligned Houthis have also imposed a naval blockade on Saudi Arabia in the Red Sea, further restricting oil export routes. A cargo vessel reported being struck by an unidentified projectile near the Strait of Hormuz off Oman’s coast, according to the UKMTO maritime security agency. Maritime sources told Reuters on Tuesday that the vessel was a dry bulk ship. Its crew had to abandon the vessel and one seafarer was missing. Iran has long demanded control over the strait, which it says it should share with Oman, which controls the opposite shore. Tehran rejected an Omani proposal last week that would have allowed shared oversight of the strait and the collection of voluntary fees from ships. A senior Iranian source said Iran is seeking full control over inbound shipping through the strait, and visibility over outbound traffic, with the ability to intervene if necessary. Giving Iran such control would be a major shift in the regional balance of power and make it more difficult for Washington to argue that “Operation Epic Fury”, which Trump launched alongside Israel in February, had weakened Washington’s longstanding foe. Questions are also growing about the sustainability of the US military campaign. The US Army has used up much of its stockpile of highly accurate long-range missiles during the war, according to three people familiar with the data, raising concerns about the military’s readiness for future conflicts. Prolonged pain Gulf officials and analysts say Iran is betting it can outlast Washington by turning the region’s trade routes, shipping lanes and energy infrastructure into pressure points that steadily raise the cost of confrontation. “Their big advantage is that they can hurt the regional states and the global economy,” said Michael Knights of the Washington Institute. Iran has publicly rejected negotiations with Washington since the collapse in early July of a memorandum of understanding the two sides signed the previous month in an attempt to end the conflict. Trump has yet to achieve the objectives he set out at the start of the war: dismantling Iran’s nuclear programme, curbing its ability to attack regional rivals and creating conditions for Iranians to overthrow their clerical rulers.

items.title: Mahama calls for right of return for global African family
items.description: President John Dramani Mahama has reiterated his call for African nations to establish a right of return for members of the global African family, saying the policy would strengthen the bond between Africa and its diaspora. The President said Ghana is considering a new legislative framework that would provide clearer pathways for residency and citizenship for members of the global African community who wish to reconnect with the continent. He said the initiative forms part of his broader vision for Africa’s future and would be among the issues he intends to advance if he becomes Chairperson of the African Union. “All African nations must have a right of return for all members of the global African family,” President Mahama stated. He said creating opportunities for people of African descent to return and participate in the continent’s development would deepen Pan-African unity and strengthen ties between Africa and the diaspora. Turning his attention to young people, President Mahama said the youth represent the generation that will shape the next chapter of Africa’s history. “Our youth are the generation that will define the next chapter of our shared history,” he said, adding that they have inherited the courage of their ancestors while benefiting from opportunities previous generations could hardly have imagined. The President said advances in technology, access to knowledge and innovation have created new possibilities for young people across Africa and the Caribbean. “Technology has connected our continents. Knowledge has become more accessible than at any time in history. Innovation has created possibilities that previous generations could only have dreamt about,” he said. He urged young people to embrace creativity, entrepreneurship and leadership, encouraging them to develop solutions that address challenges in their communities. “Be bold, lead with integrity, innovate with purpose, build enterprises that create jobs, use technology to solve problems, and serve your communities with compassion,” President Mahama advised. He expressed confidence in the ability of young Africans and members of the diaspora to transform their societies and contribute to global progress. “Our responsibility as leaders is to build societies that match your ambitions—societies founded on quality education, equal opportunity, innovation, democratic governance and shared prosperity,” he said. President Mahama said if these foundations are established, people of African descent will not only take part in shaping the future but will also lead it.

items.title: Supporting breastfeeding starts with the family: why fathers matter
items.description: When Mr. M.A.G., a 36-year-old pastor and father of a seven-month-old daughter, remembers the early weeks after his baby’s birth, he recalls more than the joy of becoming a father. He remembers waking his baby frequently, helping to feed her with expressed breast milk so that his wife, who was recovering from childbirth, could get some much-needed rest. “I started these responsibilities when my wife was healing from delivery, and subsequently, when she had to do something. My baby had to eat every two hours, and as the mother is not in the best state of health, I woke the baby up every two hours and, with the help of the breast pump, I fed the baby from the milk collected so that her mother could sleep.” For Mr. M. A.G., supporting breastfeeding meant sharing household responsibilities, caring for the baby, and ensuring that his wife had time to recover and rest. His experience highlights a role fathers can play in breastfeeding that is sometimes overlooked. They may not directly breastfeed, but they can help create the conditions that enable mothers to do so successfully. He believes workplaces and society must also recognize the significant role fathers play during the early weeks after childbirth. While extended family members provide valuable support, the active presence of a father makes a meaningful difference to the health and well-being of both mother and baby. Every August, the World Alliance for Breastfeeding Action (WABA) coordinates World Breastfeeding Week, drawing attention to the importance of breastfeeding and creating supportive environments. When mothers receive encouragement and practical support at home, they are more likely to feel confident and continue breastfeeding. For many families, that support can begin with the father. The World Health Organisation (WHO) and UNICEF recommend that breastfeeding begin within the first hour after birth, that infants receive only breast milk for the first six months, and that breastfeeding continue alongside appropriate complementary foods until two years of age or beyond. Breast milk provides complete nutrition, protects against infection, supports healthy brain development, and reduces the risk of illnesses later in life. Mothers also benefit, with a lower risk of breast and ovarian cancers, type 2 diabetes, and high blood pressure. Yet meeting breastfeeding recommendations can be challenging for many families. In Ghana, although breastfeeding is widely initiated, exclusive breastfeeding declines as infants grow older. By four to five months, only about half of babies are exclusively breastfed. Mothers may become exhausted, return to work, receive conflicting advice from relatives, or experience breastfeeding difficulties without timely professional support. These challenges make the involvement of fathers particularly important. Fathers do not need to breastfeed to be breastfeeding champions. They can offer support in simple but meaningful ways. Encouragement. New mothers often worry if they have enough milk or if their baby is feeding well. A supportive partner can give them the confidence to keep going. Helping around the house. Cooking, caring for older children, changing diapers, bathing the baby, or doing chores gives mothers time to rest. Every task a father handles lets the mother focus on breastfeeding and recovery. Become an informed advocate. Fathers who attend antenatal visits, learn and recognize common breastfeeding challenges, can encourage mothers to seek help early and prevent manageable difficulties from becoming reasons to stop breastfeeding. Discouraging harmful practices. Fathers who understand the importance of a mother’s first milk, colostrum, can ensure that their babies receive it instead of discarding colostrum or introducing water, herbal preparations, or other foods before six months of age. Studies conducted across different countries consistently show that fathers who receive breastfeeding education significantly improve the chances that mothers will start breastfeeding early, breastfeed exclusively for the first 6 months, and continue breastfeeding longer. The evidence reinforces the idea that fathers are not passive observers in infant feeding but are essential partners in their children’s nutrition and healthy development. Yet many fathers remain on the sidelines. Antenatal care and breastfeeding education often focus primarily on mothers, leaving some fathers willing to help but unsure about what they can do. Long working hours, limited paternity leave, cultural expectations, and the belief that infant feeding is solely a woman’s responsibility continue to limit fathers’ involvement. Changing this requires action from more than fathers alone. Healthcare workers should invite fathers to antenatal and postnatal visits and give them practical advice on how to support their partners with breastfeeding. 2. Employers should understand that fathers need time off to support their families after a baby is born. 3. Communities and families should encourage fathers to participate rather than observe. The 2026 World Breastfeeding Week theme, “Breastfeeding for a Sustainable Start in Life: Strengthen What Works ,” provides an opportunity to reflect on what works and how families and communities can strengthen the support systems that help mothers breastfeed. One of the simplest and most effective investments is an informed, supportive father. The message is simple. A father’s role begins long before a child can walk or speak. His encouragement, patience, practical assistance, and firm support can help create an environment in which breastfeeding is more achievable. Healthy children are not raised by mothers alone. Families nurture them, and fathers are essential partners in giving every child the healthiest possible start in life. Authors: Evelyn Aboagye is an Associate Professor of Pediatrics at University of Virginia and an International Board-Certified Lactation Consultant Iruoghene G. Solomon, Ernestina Narh-Korley and Obed A. A. Quachie are medical students at Family Health University

items.title: Mahama praises Jamaica’s Hurricane Melissa recovery, cites Ghana’s Pan-African solidarity
items.description: President John Dramani Mahama has commended the government and people of Jamaica for their resilience and swift recovery following the devastation caused by Hurricane Melissa, describing the country’s response as a reflection of the strength and determination of its people. Addressing a special joint sitting of Jamaica’s Parliament during his state visit on August 4, President Mahama said Jamaica’s ability to recover from the disaster demonstrated the nation’s enduring spirit. “Let me use this occasion to commend the Government and people of Jamaica for your resilience and for your speedy recovery after Hurricane Melissa,” he said. The President noted that the pace of recovery was remarkable, adding that visitors to Kingston could hardly recognise the extent of the destruction caused by the storm. “Since our visit here in Kingston, Jamaica, one would hardly recognise that Hurricane Melissa came through here. Jamaica has bounced back,” he stated. President Mahama said the recovery effort reflected Jamaica’s long-standing tradition of courage and resilience in the face of challenges. He also highlighted Ghana’s support for Jamaica during the difficult period, saying the response demonstrated the deep friendship and solidarity between the two countries. “When Hurricane Melissa’s widespread destruction in Jamaica occurred, Ghana responded as family,” President Mahama said. He explained that the Ghana Armed Forces Engineers Regiment was deployed to assist in reconstruction efforts, working closely with the Jamaica Defence Force, government agencies and local communities. The Ghanaian team supported efforts to restore damaged infrastructure, rehabilitate public facilities and assist families rebuilding their lives after the disaster. President Mahama said Ghana’s contribution was not simply an act of assistance but a practical expression of Pan-African solidarity. “It was not simply an engineering assignment. It was a practical demonstration of Pan-African solidarity,” he said. He praised the professionalism, discipline and selfless service of the Ghanaian personnel involved in the recovery mission, saying their actions strengthened the bond between the two nations. “Their work stands as a reminder that while the Atlantic Ocean separates our shores, it cannot separate our humanity,” President Mahama stated. He added that the relationship between Ghana and Jamaica is built on the understanding that nations must stand together during moments of hardship. “When one member of our family suffers, the others must respond. That is the spirit of Pan-Africanism. That is the essence of South-South cooperation, and that is the enduring character of the friendship between Ghana and Jamaica,” he said. President Mahama said Jamaica’s recovery after Hurricane Melissa serves as another example of the country’s resilience and its ability to overcome adversity.

items.title: Bignamou : un pasteur et son épouse tués par un accident de la route
items.description: Un tragique accident de la circulation a coûté la vie à un pasteur et à son épouse dans la soirée du lundi 3 août 2026, entre le secteur de Vologbélaye et le district de Nawei, dans la sous-préfecture de Bignamou. Selon les informations recueillies sur place, les victimes sont le pasteur Joseph Camara, en service à l'Église de Galaye, dans la commune rurale de Péla, et son épouse. Le couple revenait d'une visite familiale dans son village natal de Banzou lorsqu'il a été mortellement percuté par un pick-up en provenance de Nawei. D'après les premiers témoignages, le conducteur du véhicule aurait perdu le contrôle de son engin avant de dévier de sa trajectoire et de faucher le couple. Joint par notre rédaction, un proche de la famille, Cécé Alexis, a confirmé les circonstances du drame. Il a précisé que le pasteur Joseph Camara et son épouse séjournaient à Banzou, un district situé à une dizaine de kilomètres de Bignamou, et qu'ils avaient repris la route en direction de leur lieu de service lorsque l'accident s'est produit. Ce drame a provoqué une vive émotion au sein des familles endeuillées, de leurs proches ainsi que de la communauté chrétienne de la localité, profondément bouleversée par cette disparition brutale. Selon les informations recueillies, l'inhumation du pasteur Joseph Camara et de son épouse est prévue ce mardi 4 août 2026.

items.title: A Sibling Is Not Always a ‘Gift’
items.description: W ithin months of having her first child, Samantha Savran began hearing from family and friends that she should have a second. Doing so would be the greatest “gift” that she and her husband could give their son, people told them. At first, Savran agreed. Growing up with a brother, she had liked having a live-in playmate and confidant. But the more she thought about her situation, she grew hesitant. Her birth experience had been traumatic. And she wasn’t sure if having a sibling would be the best for her son, who was thriving. What she and her husband could offer him—Montessori preschool, a family trip to Japan—might not be possible with a second child. But she also knew that sibling relationships could turn painful. In adulthood, her connection with her brother had splintered. They had disagreements that had spiraled into a full-blown falling out, and their relationship was now “difficult,” she told me. “It’s hard to say that I still see it as a ‘gift.’” The notion that parents should give children a sibling is common. “Life Is Better With Siblings,” declared the headline on a recent New York Times op-ed by the Catholic University professor Catherine Pakaluk, who argued that, unlike small families, “large families generate moral education the way an engine generates heat.” In a column last year for The Guardian , a writer explained that she had “gifted my daughters each other,” and that doing so was a way of “quietly healing my childhood loneliness.” On social media, heartstring-tugging posts of small children holding hands and nuzzling underscore the point: “A baby brother is the universe’s way of giving a little girl her first real love story,” one mom captioned a video. When I asked online about this kind of messaging, I heard from dozens of parents who had been on the receiving end. A New York City woman who works in health care, fresh off maternity leave, said a patient had told her that she would be “selfish” not to have a second child. Scarlet de Lemeny, a recently married retail consultant based in Boston, told me that before she’d even set a wedding date, people had advised her to have multiple children—because “they need a friend.” This month, the British celebrity Kate Lawler, who has one 5-year-old, wrote in Metro : “I’m now regularly hounded with abuse when I talk about the positives of having just one, as if raising my daughter without a sibling is the cruellest thing I could possibly do.” This prodding isn’t limited to one-child parents. A mother of two boys told me that she keeps hearing she should “definitely try for a third, so you can have a girl.” The people who implore women to have more kids usually mean well. It’s lovely, and reasonable, to hope that a sibling might become a child’s lifelong friend and source of support. But the “gift” messaging isn’t always benign. For parents, it can add pressure, guilt, and anxiety to an already huge life decision—particularly for women, who in addition to giving birth tend to bear the brunt of fertility expectations, care responsibilities , and mental and physical health burdens, and to take a hit to their long-term employment and earnings prospects. The “gift” phrasing also rests on a shaky premise. People, after all, aren’t inanimate objects. They are unpredictable beings with a will and their own motivations. And not even the best of intentions can guarantee that a child will experience a new sibling as a gift. T he sibling bond can be unlike any other . I’ve heard people describe their siblings as their “first phone call,” their “life raft,” their “village.” Some siblings can finish one another’s sentences or seem to sense when something is wrong even when they’re far away, in another state. One of my friends is so close with her brother that he made her the “best ma’am” at his wedding. Another person told me that, when her parents kicked her out, her sister took her in—the same weekend the sister was getting married. Broadly, research shows that sibling relationships tend to be more positive than negative. One large, recent U.S. survey found that more than half of respondents ages 25 to 35 had “tight-knit” relationships with their full siblings. Although events such as starting their own family can cause siblings to drift apart, they typically experience a “rebound,” the sibling researcher Megan Gilligan, an associate professor at the University of Missouri, told me. In one study, a sample of older adults found that most reported warm, low-conflict sibling ties. But these bonds can be uniquely complicated. “Sibling relationships are different than our other family ties, and they tend to be more complex,” Gilligan said. “We use the term ambivalence : They can be both very positive and very negative, simultaneously.” The same factors that can make these relationships go so right—growing up together; knowing one another’s triggers, foibles, and flaws—can also make them go very wrong. When aging parents need care or die, for instance, their grown children might find benefits to sharing the costs, decision making, and emotional burden, Gilligan said. But in some families, the same situations can cause conflict and resentment. [ Read: Couples therapy, but for siblings ] Research also indicates that it isn’t simply having a sibling that benefits children—it’s having a good relationship with one. That may sound like plain common sense, but the distinction is crucial. A paper last year identified sibling aggression and abuse as “ invisible and widespread public health problems .” One watershed 2013 study found that children who endured sibling aggression, including name-calling and “mean” comments, had worse mental health than those who didn’t. Still darker and less discussed is sibling sexual abuse. There’s no way to know how common it is, Brad Watts, a Tennessee-based therapist who specializes in sibling abuse, told me. But in more than a decade of working with affected families, he has seen a theme: No family is guaranteed immunity. “It can happen in my home,” he told me. “It can happen in anybody’s home.” Watts has three boys. He has loved watching them become close friends. But he would never tell someone to “give” their child a sibling. “I can talk about all kinds of siblings that were not ‘gifts,’” Watts said. “They were, more or less, terrors.” Even close sibling relationships aren’t always beneficial. Studies over the years have found that adolescents are more likely to engage in risky behavior , such as smoking or unsafe sex, and even to break the law if another sibling did—especially if their relationship is tight. Calling a younger sibling a “gift” can create unintended consequences, too, Whitney Goodman, a Miami-based therapist, told me. Although this is surely no one’s intent, the phrasing can imply that a child has been brought into the world in the service of another. The parental preference it suggests may cause children to feel they’re treated or desired differently—one of the most common reasons sibling relationships fracture. L earning to navigate life with someone you didn’t choose to grow up with can be rewarding. But not always. The same large U.S. survey that found “tight-knit” relationships among many full siblings also found that up to one in five sibling relationships were characterized by “detachment”—meaning that siblings were less likely to have frequent contact, to feel emotionally close, or to offer one another social or financial support. In Germany, researchers looking at a nationally representative sample of nearly 6,000 adults found that 28 percent of respondents were estranged from a sibling at least once over the study’s six-year period. [ Read: The longest relationships of our lives ] De Lemeny, the Boston retail consultant, has amassed more than half a million followers across TikTok and Instagram by sharing about her life and childhood, and her experience going no-contact with her parents. Many followers ask about her brother, assuming that they must have “trauma-bonded.” When she explains that, actually, she and her brother don’t speak, some are shocked. Others thank her: They weren’t close to their siblings and thought they were alone in this. “It’s a dynamic that doesn’t really get spoken about,” de Lemeny said. “It’s something that carries a lot of shame.” This silence about conflict and estrangement can have ripple effects in the broader culture. It might lead parents-to-be to assume that, barring some grave unlikelihood, siblings will be friends for life. It also contributes to the narrative that if a person doesn’t “give” their child a sibling, they will be, unequivocally, depriving them of something important. Anna de Sapio, a social worker in the United Kingdom, gave birth during the first COVID lockdown and struggled with isolation, exhaustion, and postpartum depression and anxiety. Yet when her daughter was only four months old, de Sapio began to get the question: When are you planning to give her a sibling? It made de Sapio feel “depleted,” she told me—as if, no matter how much of herself she gave, it wasn’t enough. Nearly every mother I spoke with expressed guilt about her decision making: one-child moms for not “giving” their child a built-in best friend; multiple-child moms who after having additional kids felt awful that they had less time and attention for their first. And these days, the pressure is coming not just from friends and family but also from politicians and other public figures: Donald Trump floating “baby bonuses”; Elon Musk arguing that the “number one threat to the West” is low birth rates; tradwives, tech bros, and other proponents of the pronatalist movement who repeat over and over that having more children isn’t a lifestyle choice—it’s a moral good. Like the “moral good” rhetoric, which assumes that having more babies is all upside, the “gift” rhetoric ignores the fact that having one child may simply be the best decision for many families—including for solo children. Research spanning decades suggests that, contrary to stereotype, only children tend to be just as well-adjusted as kids in multi-child households, enjoy the same or better mental health, and have closer relationships with their parents. They are no more narcissistic, competitive, or lonely than those with siblings. And although they may possess, as very young children, slightly-less-developed interpersonal skills, these differences generally disappear over time . Plus, let’s be blunt: Regardless of how much parents love every child that they have, additional children can add stress and expense. This can affect the mental well-being of parents and, by extension, their children. Kids generally fare better when their caregivers are in good mental health , can invest more time in caregiving, and are sensitive and responsive to their child’s needs. These nuances may help explain why, on average, children with more than three or four siblings have worse mental and physical health than kids with fewer or none. The “gift” phrasing misses something else, too: When people frame siblings as gifts and being an only child as a deficit, they discount what many only-child families told me they’ve experienced: the joy that can come from having a small, tight-knit family where jealousies and conflicts are mostly absent, and parents’ time and attention are undivided. After several years of uncertainty, Savran and her husband made a decision: They would stick to having one child. “Giving the best life we can to the one kid we have,” she said, “and making sure he’s surrounded by friends and ‘framily’ and people who love him, ended up being our priority.” No one knows what a sibling might bring. But this kind of careful decision making—which takes the capacities, joys, and temperaments of already existing family members into account—can be its own gift.

items.title: Crise migratoire à Ceuta : l’UE renforce la surveillance des frontières après un afflux record
items.description: Les ministres de l'Interieur des 27 etats membres de l'Union europeenne (UE) se sont reunis ce 3 août en visioconference pour discuter de la crise migratoire a Ceuta, enclave espagnole situee dans le nord du Maroc, apres l'arrivee soudaine de pres de 72 000 migrants la semaine derniere. Selon le ministre espagnol de l'Interieur, environ 70 000 personnes ont depuis regagne le Maroc sous escorte policiere. Au total, « 75 corps de migrants morts ont ete retrouves », a-t-il indique lors de la reunion. a l'issue des echanges, le ministre francais de l'Interieur, Laurent Nuñez, a affirme que les etats membres avaient « salue la gestion espagnole de la crise » et exprime leur solidarite avec Madrid, tout en soulignant la « cooperation remarquable avec le Maroc ». Face a cet episode inedit, plusieurs mesures de renforcement du controle aux frontieres ont ete annoncees. Un « barrage flottant », destine a empecher les traversees maritimes irregulieres, a ainsi ete installe au large de Ceuta. En France, Laurent Nuñez a annonce un « renforcement significatif du controle a la frontiere franco-espagnole » afin de limiter les « mouvements secondaires ». La lutte contre les passeurs Cinq forces mobiles surveillent deja les 37 points de passage dans les Pyrenees-Orientales et les Pyrenees-Atlantiques, avant l'arrivee de 186 agents supplementaires de la Force frontiere d'intervention rapide. Le ministre francais de l'Interieur a egalement defendu le role de l'espace Schengen, estimant qu'il « n'etait pas le probleme, mais la solution ». Les Vingt-Sept ont convenu de renforcer la lutte contre les reseaux de passeurs, notamment a travers « le demantelement des reseaux dans les pays de transit » et l'amelioration des procedures de retour des migrants deboutes. Les etats membres ont par ailleurs salue la mise en œuvre prochaine du Pacte europeen sur l'asile et la migration, qui prevoit notamment un filtrage renforce aux frontieres exterieures, l'enregistrement des donnees biometriques et une reforme des procedures de retour. « Tout le monde a salue les avancees sur le reglement retour », a precise Laurent Nuñez. Concernant les traversees de la Manche vers le Royaume-Uni, le ministre francais a assure qu'elles etaient en baisse. « Depuis le debut de l'annee, le nombre de traversees reussies a ete de 160, contre 413 l'annee precedente », a-t-il declare, attribuant cette evolution a une nouvelle doctrine d'interception en mer.

items.title: Cop allegedly rapes woman inside Lahore police station; entire staff suspended
items.description: LAHORE: The entire staff of Lahore’s Ghaziabad police station was suspended on Tuesday after it emerged that an assistant sub-inspector had allegedly raped a woman on the premises on Sunday. Lahore DIG (Operations) Faisal Kamran confirmed the development to Dawn , saying that the woman was allegedly raped by an assistant sub-inspector inside a room at the police station. He said the woman had identified, in the presence of senior police officials, the exact room where she was allegedly raped. “The room was located on the upper floor of the police station,” he said. The DIG said he suspended the entire staff of the police station because, according to police rules, all of them were responsible for keeping a check on any wrongdoing at the station. “No one bothered to enquire why the ASI had brought the woman to the police station in the absence of any female personnel,” he said. Over 70 personnel and officials deployed at the police station have been suspended, according to a police report seen by Dawn . A first information report (FIR) of the incident, a copy of which is available with Dawn , was registered at Ghaziabad police station on Monday under Section 376 (punishment for rape) of the Pakistan Penal Code and 155-C of Police Order, 2002, which outlines penalties for misconduct by police officers. The FIR quotes the complainant, the woman’s father, as saying that his daughter, aged around 20 and mentally impaired, had left home in the afternoon on Sunday and did not return for a long time, following which they began searching for her. He said a man told him that a policeman, who was in civilian clothes, had taken his daughter away with him. “We then reached the Ghaziabad police station at around 9pm. But as soon as we reached there, my brother called and told me that my daughter had returned home,” he told police, adding that his daughter was crying when he reached home. When asked for the reason, she said a police official had taken her with him on a motorcycle and then raped her. Prosecutor general takes notice Punjab Prosecutor General Irfan Sadiq Tarar has taken notice of the incident, declaring it a high-profile case and directing that the investigation be conducted in a transparent, impartial and merit-based manner. According to a statement, Tarar has summoned the investigating officer to his office on Thursday, along with the complete case record for a review of the investigation. He directed that all stages of the probe be completed in accordance with the law, warning that any negligence or delay would not be tolerated. The prosecutor general also said ensuring legal protection and justice for the survivor was the prosecution department’s top priority, adding that crimes against women and children were intolerable and would be prosecuted effectively on the basis of strong evidence so that those responsible could be punished in accordance with the law.

GNL : Moscou veut prendre pied sur le marché marocain
items.description: Le développement des infrastructures marocaines de gaz naturel liquéfié (GNL) suscite l'intérêt de la Russie. Dans un entretien accordé à l'agence russe RIA Novosti, l'ambassadeur de Russie à Rabat, Igor Belyayev, voit dans cette dynamique une opportunité de renforcer la présence économique russe au Maroc, de l'énergie à l'industrie pharmaceutique, en passant par le numérique. Le développement des futurs terminaux marocains de réception et de regazéification du gaz naturel liquéfié (GNL) attire l'attention de Moscou. Dans un entretien accordé à l'agence de presse russe RIA Novosti, l'ambassadeur de Russie au Maroc, Igor Belyayev, estime que cette nouvelle infrastructure ouvrira la voie à de nouvelles opportunités de coopération entre les deux pays, tout en dévoilant les secteurs sur lesquels les entreprises russes souhaitent désormais se positionner au Royaume. Pour le diplomate, le GNL constitue aujourd'hui l'un des axes les plus prometteurs des relations énergétiques entre Rabat et Moscou. Il souligne que les projets marocains de réception et de regazéification du gaz liquéfié créeront un environnement favorable à l'arrivée de nouveaux fournisseurs sur le marché national. Sans évoquer de négociations en cours ni d'accord commercial, il estime que cette évolution offre des perspectives intéressantes pour les exportateurs russes. Cette prise de position intervient alors que le Maroc poursuit sa stratégie de diversification de ses approvisionnements énergétiques afin de renforcer sa sécurité énergétique et d'accompagner la montée en puissance des énergies renouvelables dans son mix électrique. L'hydrogène vert dans le viseur Au-delà du GNL, l'entretien met en évidence l'intérêt grandissant de la Russie pour la stratégie marocaine de transition énergétique. Selon Igor Belyayev, le développement de la filière marocaine de l'hydrogène vert ouvre de nouvelles perspectives aux entreprises russes, qui pourraient participer dans un premier temps aux projets pilotes avant de contribuer à des investissements de plus grande envergure. L'ambassadeur met notamment en avant l'expertise du groupe Rosatom, dont les activités couvrent désormais plusieurs segments liés aux énergies bas carbone, au stockage d'énergie et aux infrastructures énergétiques. Il évoque également l'intérêt du constructeur russe Power Machines pour les projets de modernisation des centrales thermiques et hydroélectriques marocaines. Autre signal de l'intérêt croissant de Moscou pour le marché marocain : le ministère russe de l'Énergie prévoit de déployer des attachés énergétiques dans plusieurs représentations diplomatiques, dont l'ambassade de Russie à Rabat, afin de renforcer les contacts avec les autorités locales et d'accompagner les entreprises russes dans leurs projets. Des ambitions qui dépassent le secteur énergétique L'entretien révèle également la volonté de Moscou d'élargir sa coopération économique avec le Royaume bien au-delà de l'énergie. Igor Belyayev rappelle que les échanges commerciaux entre les deux pays oscillent actuellement entre 1,5 et 2 milliards de dollars, un niveau qu'il juge inférieur au potentiel réel des relations bilatérales. Selon lui, plusieurs secteurs offrent des perspectives de développement. Le diplomate cite notamment l'industrie pharmaceutique, estimant que les entreprises russes disposent d'un savoir-faire reconnu dans la production de médicaments, de vaccins et de produits biotechnologiques susceptibles d'intéresser le marché marocain. Il évoque également les opportunités offertes par la stratégie Maroc Digital 2030. Selon lui, les entreprises russes spécialisées dans les logiciels, la cybersécurité, l'intelligence artificielle et les solutions numériques pourraient développer de nouveaux partenariats avec leurs homologues marocains. Le Maroc, un marché stratégique pour Moscou En filigrane, l'entretien traduit une volonté plus large de la Russie de renforcer son ancrage économique au Maroc. Qu'il s'agisse du gaz naturel liquéfié, de l'hydrogène vert, des infrastructures énergétiques, de l'industrie pharmaceutique ou encore du numérique, Moscou entend se positionner sur plusieurs chantiers structurants portés par le Royaume. Sans annoncer de nouveaux contrats ni d'accords imminents, l'ambassadeur russe présente le Maroc comme un partenaire stratégique offrant d'importantes perspectives de coopération dans des secteurs appelés à jouer un rôle majeur dans les prochaines années. The post GNL : Moscou veut prendre pied sur le marché marocain appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Police investigate deaths of two Beninese women found in Tamale hotel room
items.description: The Northern Regional Police Command has launched investigations into the deaths of two women whose bodies were discovered in a room at Cab Hospitality Hotel in the Gbewa Residential Area of Tamale. The bodies were found on Monday, August 3, after the hotel management alerted the police to the incident. In a statement issued on Tuesday, August 4, the Police said officers who responded to the report found the bodies of the two women, who are believed to be nationals of Benin. The bodies have since been conveyed to the Tamale Teaching Hospital mortuary for preservation and a post-mortem examination to determine the exact cause of death. Police said preliminary investigations are underway to establish the circumstances surrounding the deaths, formally identify the deceased and work with the relevant authorities to contact their families. To support the investigation, the Inspector-General of Police (IGP) has deployed a special team comprising investigators, intelligence officers and crime scene experts from the National Police Headquarters to assist the Northern Regional Police Command. The Police have appealed to members of the public with credible information that could aid the investigation to call the emergency numbers 191 or 18555, or report to the nearest police station.
